newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince buys 3 percent of Cordiant stock.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince buys 3 percent of Cordiant stock.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal said Tuesday he bought mroe than 3 percent of London-based advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc for 150 million riyals ($40 million).

A statement from the prince's office in the Saudi capital Riyadh said he bought the shares on the market in Britain, the latest in a recent string of international, high-profile acquisitions by the prince.

It said the prince "informed Cordiant that he now owns over 3 percent of its total share capital and that the value of the deal was 150 million Saudi riyals and the shares were bought on the market in Britain."
"I think the Cordiant management has done a very good job so far to improve the performance of the company," the prince said in the statement.
The statement said Cordiant's Chief Executive Bob Seelert welcomed the acquisition by the prince, who has a wide-ranging international portfolio including banks and hotels.

Cordiant, the holding company formerly known as Saatchi & Saatchi, said in April it planned to split its Saatchi & Saatchi and Bates advertising agencies and Zenith media planning and buying operation into three independently managed businesses.
The statement from the prince's office said the 40-year-old nephew of Saudi King Fahd has been a long-time Saatchi & Saatchi client.
His purchase of the Cordiant shares was the latest in a series of international acquisitions and deals in the last three months.
In March and April he announced he had bought 5 percent of Apple Computer Inc., 5 percent of Trans World Airlines Inc. and 5 percent of Norwegian Cruise Lines.
Last month, the prince and Planet Hollywood formed a strategic pact in which the prince would develop up to 34 Planet restaurant-merchandise units in 23 countries.

Though not huge compared to the prince's other holdings, the new investments are part of a new business trend of diversifying investments away from real estate and entertainment, the prince told Reuters in April.
He controls a portfolio that includes banks, an investment chain, a broadcasting operation and huge property holdings including the Fairmont and Four Seasons hotel chains.

He has shares in U.S. banking giant Citicorp, retailer Saks Fifth Avenue, the Plaza Hotel, the Euro Disney theme park near Paris and Canary Wharf in London's Docklands. He also has stakes in former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's television and advertising business Mediaset.
Last year he signed a deal with popstar Michael Jackson to cooperate on concerts, films, television, fun parks and hotels.
